albums.blurb: Bob James's first album for Creed Taylor's CTI label, recorded at Rudy Van Gelder's studio in early 1974 after years spent arranging for Sarah Vaughan and Quincy Jones. Its six instrumental tracks set Fender Rhodes and orchestral arrangements over funk rhythm sections, reworking Pachelbel and Mussorgsky alongside originals; the closer "Nautilus" became one of the most sampled recordings in hip-hop, turning up in tracks by Run-D.M.C., Eric B. & Rakim, A Tribe Called Quest and Ghostface Killah.
albums.reception: One reached number 2 on Billboard's Top Jazz Albums chart in 1974 and also crossed over to the pop and soul album charts.

albums.blurb: The debut studio album from the Colombian-American singer, following her 2015 mixtape Por Vida. Across fifteen tracks it slides between doo-wop, reggaeton, funk and psychedelic soul, with contributions from Thundercat, Tyler, the Creator, Bootsy Collins, Steve Lacy and Damon Albarn, led by the single "After the Storm".
albums.reception: Isolation holds a Metacritic score of 87 out of 100 based on 17 critic reviews, and NME gave it a five-star review.

albums.blurb: Mild High Club is the project of Los Angeles multi-instrumentalist Alexander Brettin, who records for Stones Throw. Skiptracing, his second album, is a loose concept record about a detective tracing the sound and spirit of American music, built from soft-focus jazz chords, tape-warped keyboards and Steely Dan-indebted harmony; Brettin followed it in 2017 with Sketches of Brunswick East, a collaboration with King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard.
albums.reception: Skiptracing scored 68 out of 100 on Metacritic, indicating generally favorable reviews, with Exclaim! rating it 8/10 and Record Collector four stars out of five.
